---
title: "Results, Provenance, and Packaging"
---

A benchmark that cannot be reviewed is a demo. MLPerf EDU treats the artifacts
of a run as first-class products, designed to be handed to an instructor, an
artifact evaluation committee, or a co-author.

## The Four Artifacts

Every workload run emits four files, named after the workload and profile:

| **Artifact** | **Role** |
|:---|:---|
| `*_report.json` | The complete result with metrics, environment fingerprint, asset dossiers, and quality status |
| `*_report.html` | The default dashboard with the lead result, target decision, configuration, lineage, and provenance |
| `*_report.csv` | Flat metrics for spreadsheets and plotting |
| `*.provd.json` | The provenance artifact: SHA-256 hashes of model state and assets |

The `.provd` artifact binds a result to its recorded inputs and environment.
For training workloads it can capture the frozen model `state_dict` hash.
Inference workloads can declare and verify a shared checkpoint dependency.
Verification proves that the recorded files match the manifest; it does not by
itself establish benchmark validity or MLCommons acceptance.

## Reading the Dashboard

The lead view is derived from the report rather than a fixed profile layout. A
functional-only report shows a readiness meter, passed or failed paths, and
clearly secondary diagnostic values. A quality-bearing report shows target
decisions and a direction-aware attainment bar where 100% means the declared
gate. A mixed report keeps separate readiness and quality meters so setup
success cannot hide a missed quality target.

Raw benchmark values are not combined into one cross-workload chart. Accuracy,
FID, loss, AUC, and pass@1 use different units and improve in different
directions. The normalized target-attainment view supports valid comparison
without implying that the raw metrics share a scale. Distribution charts belong
to the later stability view and appear only when repeated run evidence exists.

The remaining sections preserve the context needed to interpret each result.
Run Configuration records the exact mode, phase, backend, device, seed, and
workload settings. Model Lineage distinguishes a locally trained checkpoint
from an upstream pretrained checkpoint and follows it through inference and
evaluation. Provenance links the JSON report, manifest, run fingerprint, and
checkpoint digest.

The suite health report is a second, intentionally smaller view. `mlperf
health` runs every registered `min` path, verifies the manifests, and groups
functional results by suite. It never places a min diagnostic beside a max
quality target. Instead, each row says that quality was not evaluated and
links to the detailed run artifacts.

## Reading and Converting Reports

```bash
uv run mlperf report submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max_report.json
uv run mlperf report submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max_report.json --format html --open
uv run mlperf report submissions/current/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --baseline submissions/baseline/image-classification_max_report.json \
  --format html --open
uv run mlperf report submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max_report.json --format csv
uv run mlperf report submissions --format html --open                    # latest in a directory
```

Pointing `report` at a directory picks up the most recent run, which avoids
copying timestamped filenames.

An explicit `--baseline` adds a comparison section to JSON and HTML output.
Quality values are compared only when the workload, profile, mode, phase,
dataset, evaluator, and target contract match. Performance bars and improvement
percentages require the same checkpoint lineage and complete comparison
fingerprint as well. The dashboard lists the mismatched boundary when a
comparison is invalid. See the
[result comparison example](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/tree/main/mlperf-edu/examples/result-comparison)
for a compatible rerun and an intentionally blocked batch-size change.

## Verifying and Packaging a Submission

```bash
uv run mlperf verify submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max.provd.json
uv run mlperf package submissions/causal-language-modeling_training_max.provd.json
```

`verify` re-checks the provenance manifest, including its hashes and recorded
quality status. `package` bundles a verified result into a portable submission
archive for grading or artifact review. Release CI checks verification again
after clean extraction.

## What the Fingerprint Buys You

Reports embed the hardware and software fingerprint of the machine that
produced them, including Python, PyTorch, platform, and accelerator details.
Matching profiles and disclosed fingerprints are necessary for comparison,
but they are not sufficient. The workload, mode, phase, quality result, dataset
recipe, checkpoint lineage, and release-validation state must also match.

The fingerprint distinguishes an availability-detected backend from the
report-selected backend that executed the workload. Its comparison digest binds
CPU topology, accelerator runtime and driver metadata when discoverable,
PyTorch threading and numeric policies, deterministic and benchmark flags, and
an explicit allowlist of performance-related environment settings. If a report
declares precision or compilation mode, the run comparison digest binds those
selections as well.
